arxiv-1806-00468.title: Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent on Linear Convolutional Networks
arxiv-1806-00468.creator: Suriya Gunasekar, Jason D. Lee, Daniel Soudry, Nathan Srebro
arxiv-1806-00468.description: Abstract We show that gradient descent on full width linear convolutional networks of depth L L converges to a linear predictor related to the ℓ 2 / L \ell_{2/L} bridge penalty in the frequency domain. This is in contrast to fully connected linear networks, where regardless of depth, gradient descent converges to the ℓ 2 \ell_{2} maximum margin solution.

arxiv-1809-06094.title: Collective search with finite perception: transient dynamics and search efficiency
arxiv-1809-06094.creator: Adam Gosztolai, Jose A. Carrillo, Mauricio Barahona
arxiv-1809-06094.description: Abstract Motile organisms often use finite spatial perception of their surroundings to navigate and search their habitats. Yet standard models of search are usually based on purely local sensory information. To model how a finite perceptual horizon affects ecological search, we propose a framework for optimal navigation that combines concepts from random walks and optimal control theory.

arxiv-1910-02440.title: Efficacy of Haptic Pedal Feel Compensation on Driving with Regenerative Braking
arxiv-1910-02440.creator: Umut Caliskan Volkan Patoglu
arxiv-1910-02440.description: Abstract We study the efficacy of haptic pedal feel compensation on driving safety and performance during regenerative braking. In particular, we evaluate the effectiveness of the preservation of the natural brake pedal feel under two-pedal cooperative braking and one-pedal driving scenarios, through human subject experiments in a simulated vehicle pursuit task.

arxiv-2009-05689.creator: Pratik Vernekar, Zhongkui Wang, Andrea Serrani, and Kevin Passino
arxiv-2009-05689.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Pratik Vernekar, Zhongkui Wang, Andrea Serrani, and Kevin Passino. arxiv-2112-09727.title: Rank4Class: A Ranking Formulation for Multiclass Classification
arxiv-2112-09727.creator: Nan Wang, Zhen Qin, Le Yan, Honglei Zhuang, Xuanhui Wang, Michael Bendersky, Marc Najork
arxiv-2112-09727.description: Abstract Multiclass classification (MCC) is a fundamental machine learning problem of classifying each instance into one of a predefined set of classes. In the deep learning era, extensive efforts have been spent on developing more powerful neural embedding models to better represent the instance for improving MCC performance.

arxiv-2204-09772.title: A Hierarchical Bayesian Approach to Inverse Reinforcement Learning with Symbolic Reward Machine
arxiv-2204-09772.creator: Weichao Zhou, Wenchao Li
arxiv-2204-09772.description: Abstract A misspecified reward can degrade sample efficiency and induce undesired behaviors in reinforcement learning (RL) problems. We propose symbolic reward machines for incorporating high-level task knowledge when specifying the reward signals. Symbolic reward machines augment existing reward machine formalism by allowing transitions to carry predicates and symbolic reward outputs.

pmc-11283649.creator: Qiang Zhang, Zhi Chen, Yujie Chen, Zhouyang Jiang, Wenyan Li, Yingpei Li, Zhuo Yao, Wenchao Fu, Yanyu Fang, Mo Li, Yin Niu
pmc-11283649.description: Introduction:A spot sign on computed tomography angiography (CTA) scan is a widely recognized radiographic indicator of primary intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) used to predict early hematoma expansion. Nonetheless, recent multicenter studies have indicated that its predictive value for hematoma expansion is not as significant as previously stated. Therefore, identifying the reasons for the poor performance of these studies is imperative.

pmc-11418562.description: AbstractPurposeProspective, multicentric observational cohort study in Switzerland investigating measures to prevent mother-to-child transmission in pregnant women with HIV (WWH) and assessing health and development of their exposed children as well as of children with HIV (CWH) in general.ParticipantsBetween January 1986 and December 2022, a total of 1446 mother–child pairs were enrolled.

pmc-11490759.creator: Bak Zaibah Fazal, Nurshafrina Aida Yahya, Clemente Michael Wong Vui Ling, Yew Chee Wei, Thean Chor Leow, Mardani Abdul Halim, Krishnan Nair Balakrishnan, Cahyo Budiman, Zarina Amin
pmc-11490759.description: Hot springs are known to harbor potentially unique microorganisms due to the extreme temperatures in which they thrive and their biotechnologically important enzymes that are active at high temperature, which are beneficial for various industries. Sabah, Malaysia, houses several hot springs, yet knowledge of their microbiological diversity remains limited.

pmc-11611769.title: Prevalence and outcomes of germline pathogenic variants of homologous recombination repair genes in ovarian cancer
pmc-11611769.creator: Maiko Miwa, Masakazu Kitagawa, Yuka Asami, Mayumi Kobayashi‐Kato, Takafumi Watanabe, Aiko Ogasawara, Kengo Hiranuma, Hisamori Kato, Motonobu Saito, Yohei Miyagi, Tomoyasu Kato, Hiroshi Yoshida, Yukihide Momozawa, Takashi Kohno, Kouya Shiraishi, Kosei Hasegawa
pmc-11611769.description: Germline pathogenic variants (PVs) are pivotal in gynecological oncology. We focused on the prevalence, clinicopathological features, and survival impact of homologous recombination repair (HRR) PVs in patients with epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC). This was a multicenter retrospective cohort study, and 1248 patients with EOC were registered.

pmc-11625348.title: Factors Associated with Loss to Follow-Up in Pediatric Concussion Patients after Initial Visit: A Retrospective Study at a Concussion Clinic
pmc-11625348.creator: Emilia Núñez-Peña, Ryan P Kelly, Santiago Campos, Maria C Diaz, Pamela A Castillo, Shivangi Kataria, Alexia M Perez, Maria Dolores Beletanga, Alcy R Torres
pmc-11625348.description: ObjectiveThe objective of this retrospective study is to identify factors associated with loss to follow-up for postconcussion clearance in pediatric patients by comparing loss to follow-up and full clearance patients.Study designThis retrospective single-center cohort study analyzed 140 consecutive patients at a pediatric concussion clinic of a safety-net hospital for loss to follow-up, defined as not achieving clearance at last appointment.

pmc-11713885.title: Social environment of people living with dementia: Characteristics, facilitators and barriers
pmc-11713885.creator: Hanna Lea Knecht, Francisca S Rodriguez
pmc-11713885.description: BackgroundThe number of people with dementia increases worldwide. Previous studies have shown that social integration and high‐quality social relationships are beneficial for reducing dementia risk and improving symptoms. Our project aimed at identifying characteristics of the social environment of people with dementia (PWD) and their relevance for PWDs’ wellbeing, and at determining facilitators and barriers of the PWD’s social integration.

pmc-12580848.title: Advocating for incorporating public veterinary health care into human health systems
pmc-12580848.creator: Laurie Meythaler-Mullins, Cheryl Eia, Allyce H. Lobdell, Danielle M. Frey
pmc-12580848.description: In the first study to examine veterinary services in rural Alaska, this paper focuses on the use of a public health veterinary program embedded in the human health care system as a means of improving human health, specifically in rural villages such as the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta of Alaska (YK Delta).
